newsitem.title: ITALY: France is Italy's ally in EU unification - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: France is Italy's ally in EU unification - Prodi.

text.p: France has become Italy's closest ally in the fight for European unification, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in an interview with La Repubblica newspaper published on Friday.

Prodi said that the new Socialist French government had adopted similar policies to his own centre-left coalition over the question of unemployment in the build- up to the launch of the single European currency.
"Regarding the process of European unification, France is now our best ally," Prodi said.
European Union leaders earlier this week at a summit in Amsterdam agreed to put economic growth and employment at the top of their political agenda after pressure from the new French administration.
However at the same time the leaders decided to stick to original plans, promoted by the Germans, demanding fiscal austerity for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Prodi said that most newspapers seemed to think that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had gained the upper hand over the French in Amsterdam. "But I have my doubts," he added.

"Certainly (French Prime Minister Lionel) Jospin has won greater freedom of movement and his appeal over the question of employment is along the same lines as the one I made at the Florence EU summit in June 1996, which was then scotched by Kohl but has now been accepted by him," Prodi said.
